findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the sani bucket of bleach to be 10 ppm when tested with chlorine test strips. Discussed with PIC. Ensure sani buckets are frequently changed out in order to maintain concentration. Bleach: 50 to 200 ppm. Facility has test strips to check sani bucket concentrations. Bucket was remade - 200 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. 

On arrival, five containers of gravy are observed in individual containers on the counter. PIC indicated that they were cooling from breakfast. The procedure at the time is to wait for the pans to cool until they can be removed from the steam tables, portion into individual containers (or gallon bags), cooler to rom temperature and then be placed in the walk-in cooler. A conversation took place with the PIC that emphasized the importance of active cooling once foods reach 135F. Foods should cool from 135F to 70F in two hours and from 70F to 41F in four hours. These time/temperature benchmarks must be met and a time marking system should be in place to verify that cooling is being managed effectively. The items were believed to be approximately 45 minutes into the 135F to 70F point, so no violation is being noted for cooling today. Items were moved into the walk in cooler during the inspection to correct and time marks will be added to the same tags as the date marks moving foreword. Multiple hand outs given during the inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Per the PIC, there are approximately 6 part time employees that handle food in the facility on top of the CFPM each day. No reporting agreements available during this inspection. Copies of the SCDPH reporting agreements were given to the PIC to be filled out. Follow up in 10 days.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. 

No manner of verification is valuable for ensuring that the dish machine causes dishes to reach critical sanitizing temperatures in the machine. Both single use strips as well as reusable maximum registering thermometers were discussed and examples shown from the inspector’s inspection kit. Follow up in 10 days.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12 (P) Multiple employees were observed using their bare hands to turn of the faucet after hand washing. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to conduct education with employees.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) (Pf) The blade of the can opener in the kitchen area was visibly soiled with food debris during the inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the can opener cleaned during the inspection.
